author: radarph_media
text: A doctor and fitness enthusiast Fit Francis shares his collision encounter with a Green GSM taxi driver at Aurora Boulevard in Cubao, Quezon City. He also shares about how he assessed the driver and attempted to save him. While Francis was near the stoplight, he noticed that someone bumped into the back of his car. Afterwards, he checked on the vehicle and assessed the situation. "Pagbaba ko, nakita ko yung sasakyan. Ano 'to yung green taxi, yung EV. Nakita ko paatras siya, kaya sabi ko 'hala tatakbuhan pa ata ako nito.' Tapos na-realize ko, medyo malayo na yung inaatrasan niya hanggang meron na siyang naatrasang isang sasakyan," Francis said. He saw the driver's body unconsciously lying at the passenger seat, saying that the driver had a myocardial infarction (or heart attack) and acute coronary syndrome, a condition caused by sudden, reduced blood flow to the heart. After seeking help from the ambulance and the police, he made chest compressions to the driver—making him temporarily conscious on their way to the hospital. The driver requested to call his children to ask about his condition, however, he eventually passed away. Francis adds that the accident serves as a lesson for all medical doctors. "Siguro para ma-share na rin sa lahat ng mga doctors, na di natin alam kung kailan tayo tatawagin ng situation para gawin yung training na meron tayo," he added. Report by Gwyneth Nolasco #radarPH

text: DISASTER RESPONSE UPDATE| 𝐌𝐌𝐃𝐑𝐑𝐌𝐂 𝐑𝐄𝐏𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐒 𝟕𝟗.𝟔% 𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐓𝐀𝐈𝐍𝐌𝐄𝐍𝐓 𝐎𝐅 𝐍𝐀𝐕𝐎𝐓𝐀𝐒 𝐒𝐀𝐍𝐈𝐓𝐀𝐑𝐘 𝐋𝐀𝐍𝐃𝐅𝐈𝐋𝐋 𝐅𝐈𝐑𝐄 The Metro Manila Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (MMDRRMC) convened today to provide a status update on the Navotas Sanitary Landfill fire incident, reporting that the fire is now 79.6% contained. In a press briefing, MMDA Chairman and concurrent MMDRRMC head Atty. Don Artes said the discussion focused on the situation on the ground, ongoing actions, and the equipment being utilized to effectively address the issue. “Moving forward, the incident will serve as a learning experience to improve preparedness and response capabilities,” Artes stressed. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. instructed Department of National Defense (DND) Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. to seek technical assistance from foreign partners, including expert teams from Japan and the United States, to address the Navotas Sanitary Landfill fire. “The DND chief reached out to our foreign partners, who promptly responded and committed to providing continued support for the needs of Navotas,” said Special Envoy for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) Maria Antonia Yulo-Loyzaga. For his part, Navotas City Mayor John Rey Tiangco expressed his gratitude to the MMDA for convening the meeting. “I am thankful to Chairman Artes for convening this meeting. To provide a status update, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) reported that the air quality index in Metro Manila remains within acceptable or normal levels despite the recent incident involving the sanitary landfill. Additionally, we are utilizing a drone with thermal imaging capability to assess the possibility of ignition within the 44-hectare site,” Tiangco said. The mayor explained that the closure and rehabilitation plan had not been implemented by the operator, constituting violations of the conditions stipulated in the Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC). Metro Manila Council President and San Juan City Mayor Francis Zamora commended the Navotas LGU for its swift action to contain the fire. “We understand how severe the situation in Navotas has been. It should serve as a lesson for us to be more prepared instead of merely reacting,” Zamora said. The NSLF Task Group, led by the local government unit of Navotas, continues to conduct fire suppression operations through soil covering, smothering, and misting. The fire at the Navotas Sanitary Landfill began on April 10, and continuous to be actively managed. Among the agencies assisting in the operations are the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of Transportation (DOTr), DENR-Environmental Management Bureau, and MMDA. text: “PAANO NAKAPAGLABAS NG ₱75 MILLION NA NAKA-MALETA?” Ito ang reaksyon ni dating Comelec at COA Commissioner Atty. Rowena Guanzon kaugnay ng kontrobersiyal na ₱350 milyong extortion case na kinasasangkutan ng inarestong PGMN founder na si Franco Mabanta kay dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Sa kanyang social media post, kinuwestiyon ni Guanzon ang ulat na umano’y may ₱75 milyong naibigay bilang paunang bayad sa extortion operation. “Kala ko naka freeze ang mga pera at ari-arian ni Martin Looter King?” “Paano nakapaglabas ng 75 Million na naka-male maleta? Literal na MALE MALETANG PERA talaga ha, ano yun coins only?” Kinuwestiyon din ni Guanzon ang umano’y pinagmulan ng malaking halaga ng pera habang hinihintay pa umano niya ang kabuuang detalye ng kaso. “Hindi ko pa alam ang full picture sa extortion daw dahil mamaya pa ang prescon ng NBI at di pa nakakapagsalita ang mga abogado ni Franco.” Inamin din ni Guanzon na nagkaroon siya ng programa sa Peanut Gallery Media Network (PGMN), ngunit iginiit niyang hindi umano siya makikipagkompromiso kay Romualdez. “Nagka programa ako sa PGMN, totoo pero never ako makikipagcompromise kay Martin Looter hanggang dulo dahil sagad sa buto ang kasamaan ng tao na ‘yan!” “Na sa tuwing may malakas na bagyo at tataas na naman ang mga tubig dahil ghost nga ang flood control project na sana ay poprotekta sa taumbayan sa baha ay maraming buhay ang nawala, mga ari-arian na pinaghirapan ng ordinaryong Pilipino ang nasira. Mga alagang hayop ang namatay dahil sa kasakiman nila sa salapi.” “Sobrang dami ng pera pero kulang pa rin.” Dumating ang naturang pahayag matapos arestuhin ng National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) si Franco Mabanta at ilan pa niyang kasamahan sa isang entrapment operation sa Pasig City kaugnay ng umano’y tangkang pangingikil ng ₱350 milyon kay dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Ayon sa mga awtoridad, hinihingi umano ni Mabanta ang naturang halaga kapalit ng hindi pagpapalabas ng isang video na umano’y nag-uugnay kay Romualdez sa kontrobersiya ng flood control projects.

author: theydied4us
text: Hero of the Month - LCDR Radcliffe “Pete” Denniston Jr., USN Lieutenant Commander Radcliffe “Pete” Denniston Jr. was born on February 5, 1916, in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin. A graduate of Lawrence College, he entered the Navy as an aviation cadet in 1936 and trained at Pensacola, Florida before joining Torpedo Squadron Five (VT-5) aboard the USS Yorktown (CV-5). When the Pacific front of WWII opened, Denniston participated in strikes against the Gilbert and Marshall Islands, Salamaua, Lae, and Tulagi. His most distinguished actions came during the Battle of the Coral Sea in May 1942, where he successfully scored torpedo hits on two Japanese carriers while facing intense anti-aircraft fire and enemy fighter opposition. For his extraordinary heroism during the attacks at Tulagi Harbor and Coral Sea, he was awarded the Navy Cross. Following the battle of Coral Sea, Denniston returned to Fort Lauderdale, Florida as an instructor and later became chief flight instructor. On September 25, 1943, he assumed command of Torpedo Squadron Eleven (VT-11). During his second combat tour, he took part in missions against Okinawa, Formosa, Luzon, Leyte, and the Second Battle of the Philippine Sea. On November 13, 1944, while leading a glide-bombing attack against enemy shipping in Manila Harbor, his aircraft encountered heavy anti-aircraft fire. Denniston’s final transmission was: “Plane hit, am going in.” He was never seen again. LCDR Denniston is buried at the ABMC Manila American Cemetery in the Philippines. author: EwetoEdema
text: A poor student spent a night with her wealthy boss to pay her brother’s hospital bills, and that decision changed her life forever... Sofía Alvarez had gone two days without sleep. Her younger brother, Julian, was admitted to San Gabriel Medical Center after a motorcycle accident, and with each passing hour, the debt for the emergency surgeries grew. The young woman, a business administration student and intern at Torres & Associates, had tried everything: student loans, salary advances, even selling the few valuable possessions she owned. Nothing was enough. The night before, in a desperate move, she had mustered the courage to request a meeting with the company’s CEO, Alejandro Torres, a man known for his relentless seriousness and obsessive perfectionism. She had never interacted with him beyond polite nods in the elevator. But that night, Alejandro’s gaze changed when he heard Sofía’s trembling voice explaining her situation. Alejandro didn’t respond immediately. He walked to the window of his office, overlooking the glittering city lights of Manila. Then, without looking at her, he said in a tone too cold: — I can help you. But I need something in return. The proposal was clear. Raw. Humiliating. Just one night. A transaction Sofía never imagined accepting. But the image of Julian hooked up to tubes, the doctors pressuring her for decisions, and the absolute lack of options broke her resolve. That night, Sofía set aside her dignity to save her brother. The next morning, she woke up in the businessman’s private apartment. He was still asleep. On the table lay an envelope: the hospital receipt and a short note, written in his impeccable handwriting: — You owe me nothing. Consider this matter closed. Sofía felt a mixture of relief, shame, and anger. She dressed quietly, left the note exactly where she found it, and left without looking back. She thought that would be the end—a chapter buried in the darkest corner of her memory. But it wasn’t. Two weeks later, while preparing reports at the office, she received an email from Human Resources: “Urgent meeting with the CEO. 10:00 AM.” Her heart began to pound so hard she could almost hear it. She feared he wanted to bring up that night—or worse, demand more. She thought about resigning. About running away. About faking illness. She did none of those things. At 10:00 sharp, she entered Alejandro’s office. He looked at her with an expression she had never seen before: a mix of doubt, tension, and… guilt? —Sofía, I need to talk to you, —he said, locking the door behind her. The real twist had not yet begun. author: kalikasan101
text: 🌳🪾“57,000 seedlings.” 🪾🌳- Madami at magandang pakinggan. Magandang headline din. Pero hindi nito agad mapapalitan ang ecological function ng 600 mature trees na pinutol sa Metro Manila. 🪵🪵🪵🪵🪵 Sa panahon ng matinding urban heat, climate anxiety, at lumalalang pagbaha, ang mature trees ay hindi dekorasyon o obstruction sa infrastructure. Silent public servants sila ng lungsod. Libre silang nagpapalamig. Sumisipsip ng tubig-ulan. Nagfi-filter ng polusyon. Nagbabawas ng stress. Nagbibigay ng dignidad sa paglalakad sa siyudad. Ang problema sa maraming development framework ngayon: masyadong nakatingin sa quantity kaysa ecological integrity. Seedlings are future possibilities. Mature trees are present protection. Hindi linear ang kapalit. Hindi puwedeng spreadsheet mentality lang ang environmental governance. Ilang dekada bago maabot ng seedlings ang parehong canopy cover, carbon storage, cooling effect, at biodiversity support ng mature trees? Ilan ang mabubuhay? Ilan ang matatamaan ulit ng susunod na road widening? Ilan ang tunay na maitatanim sa highly urbanized spaces? Ito ang delikadong kultura ng “offset mentality” — puwedeng sirain ngayon basta may ipapangakong kapalit bukas. Pero sa climate crisis, delayed ecological recovery is also social injustice. Ang pinaka-apektado sa pagkawala ng urban trees ay hindi ang naka-aircon. Kundi ang commuter, street vendor, traffic enforcer, delivery rider, estudyante, at ordinaryong mamamayang direktang niluluto ng urban heat. At malinaw na panahon na upang paghiwalayin ang regulatory at environmental protection functions sa loob ng DENR. Hindi puwedeng iisang sistema ang parehong nagpo-promote, nag-aapprove, at dapat nagpo-protekta sa kalikasan. Kapag magkalaban ang mandato, kadalasan talo ang ecological integrity. Ang tunay na sustainable city hindi lang measured sa dami ng kalsada at bilis ng sasakyan. Sinusukat din ito sa dami ng punong nananatili, kalidad ng hangin, walkability, biodiversity, at kapasidad ng lungsod na protektahan ang buhay sa gitna ng climate extremes. Kapag mature trees ang unang sinasakripisyo para sa “development,” kailangang tanungin: development para kanino? 🌿🏙️🔥 #ProtectUrbanTrees #ClimateJustice #LaudatoSi #ManilaNeedsTrees Photo credit: Manila Times / Mike Alquinto

author: LaudatoSiPH
text: 🌳 MANILA CAN’T BREATHE ON SEEDLINGS ALONE 🔥 600 mature trees lost today cannot be replaced overnight by promises for tomorrow. “Nature cannot be regarded as something separate from ourselves or as a mere setting in which we live.” — Laudato Si’, §139 Living Laudato Si’ Philippines expresses deep concern over the continued cutting of mature trees in Metro Manila in the name of infrastructure expansion and urban development. In a city already suffering from extreme heat, worsening floods, air pollution, traffic congestion, and shrinking public green spaces, the removal of hundreds of full-grown trees represents more than ecological loss. It is a climate justice, public health, and human dignity issue. The narrative that tens of thousands of seedlings can simply compensate for the destruction of mature urban trees dangerously misunderstands ecological integrity. Seedlings are future possibilities. Mature trees are present protection. Established trees already provide critical ecosystem services: cooling urban temperatures, absorbing floodwaters, filtering pollutants, storing carbon, reducing stress, supporting biodiversity, and creating more humane and livable public spaces. These functions cannot be immediately restored through compensatory planting programs that may take decades before reaching ecological maturity. As climate impacts intensify, urban trees must be recognized not as obstacles to development, but as essential living infrastructure for climate adaptation and resilience. A truly sustainable city cannot be measured solely by road widening, elevated expressways, or faster vehicle mobility while simultaneously making urban life hotter, harsher, and less walkable for ordinary citizens. Living Laudato Si’ Philippines likewise reiterates the urgent need to separate the DENR’s regulatory and environmental protection functions. Ecological protection should never compete with project approval within the same institutional framework. The future of Manila will not only be defined by what is built, but by what society chooses to protect. 🌿🏙️ #ProtectUrbanTrees #LaudatoSi #ClimateJustice

author: father_rmv
text: Blessed Bartolomé Díaz Laurel was a Franciscan lay brother, missionary, nurse, and martyr whose life bridged the New World and the perilous mission fields of Asia in the early seventeenth century. Born around 1590 in El Puerto de Santa María, Spain, near Cádiz, he moved young to Mexico, where many sources describe him as a Mexican Franciscan. Before entering religious life he worked as a sailor, gaining practical skills and a resilient spirit that would serve him well in distant lands. In 1617 he joined the Order of Friars Minor in Valladolid (now Morelia), Mexico, professing as a lay brother. Drawn to missionary work, he was sent to the Philippines in 1619. There he spent several years in Manila, serving as a nurse in a hospital, studying the Japanese language, and preparing for the dangerous task ahead. His combination of medical care and catechesis made him especially effective among the sick and the curious. In 1623 or shortly after, Brother Bartolomé sailed for Japan with Father Francisco de Santa María. At that time Japan had begun its brutal suppression of Christianity under the Tokugawa shogunate. Undeterred, he worked quietly as a nurse and catechist, tending to the physical and spiritual needs of hidden Christians. His humility, charity, and tireless service earned him deep respect among the faithful. Arrested in the spring of 1627 during a wave of persecutions, he was imprisoned, tried for violating anti-Christian laws, and condemned to death. On August 17, 1627, in Nagasaki, he was burned alive at the stake along with companions. Witnesses noted his patience and prayerfulness even as the slow fire consumed him. He was beatified by Pope Pius IX in 1867 together with other Japanese martyrs. Though little known outside specialized hagiography, Blessed Bartolomé Díaz Laurel embodies the quiet courage of countless Franciscan lay missionaries. A sailor turned brother, a nurse turned martyr, he crossed oceans not for glory but to bring healing and faith to the farthest edges of the known world.

author: MMDA
text: Huli sa CCTV: Illegal Dumping sa Estero De Sunog Apog Natiketan ng MMDA ang isang indibidwal dahil sa iligal na pagtatapon ng basura sa Estero de Sunog Apog, Barangay 177, Tondo, Manila, ngayong araw, May 25, 9 am. Sa report ng MMDA Health, Public Safety, and Environmental Protection Office, huli sa akto ang pagtatapon ng basura ng nabanggit na indibidwal diretso sa estero. Sa tulong ng mga opisyal ng barangay, mabilis na natukoy ang violator at inisyuhan siya ng Environmental Violation Receipt (EVR). Inamin naman ng violator ang kanyang pagkakamali at nagbayad ng multa na nagkakahalaga ng P500 dahil sa kanyang paglabag sa anti-littering law. Nagbabala naman si MMDA General Manager Nicolas Torre III na nakabantay ang mga CCTV cameras ng ahensiya sa mga kalsada, estero, at kanal. Paalala sa lahat: Hindi tapunan ng basura ang estero. Maging responsable at sumunod sa regulasyon para sa kalinisan ng kapaligiran. #mmda #mmdaatyourservice
